display_title: Validating an NLP Coding-Assist Model for KC-135 Maintenance Records
one_liner: A fine-tuned ModernBERT-large model that suggests the Work Unit Code for a KC-135 maintenance record, at 0.903 top-1 and 0.978 top-3 accuracy on held-out records.
problem: Maintainers hand-assign one of roughly 1,300 Work Unit Codes to every KC-135 maintenance record. Miscoded records reduce the quality of reliability, sustainment and readiness analysis built on that data.
approach: I merged and deduplicated records from two extracts covering 2019 to 2026, then fed the discrepancy and corrective-action text to a ModernBERT-large classifier over 1,251 codes, trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and hierarchical system and subsystem auxiliary losses. I evaluated the served model on held-out records, reporting accuracy separately from label coverage, calibration by confidence band, and errors broken down by the WUC hierarchy.
decision_relevance: Supports the WUC coding decision on completed maintenance records. The top-3 suggestions plus a confidence band send low-confidence records to QC review. The confusion pairs found (for example, codes used interchangeably across bases) are direct feedback to data owners on inconsistent coding that distorts downstream analysis.

headline_results.claim: Top-1 accuracy 0.903 (95% CI 0.899-0.908) and top-3 0.978 on a 15,636-record held-out test split
98.3% of predictions land in the correct aircraft system; 63% of the remaining errors are same-subsystem near misses
Predictions shown at 70% confidence or higher, which is 93% of answerable records, are correct 94.6% of the time (n = 14,795)
Re-measuring what the app actually served caught a train/serve pooling mismatch that had cut production accuracy from 0.897 to 0.756 for three months
Flat and hierarchical variants are statistically indistinguishable (sign test p = 0.33), so the simpler one ships

limitations: Accuracy is scored against QC-pipeline labels from the same process that produced the training labels. It has not been checked by a KC-135 subject-matter expert (a 25-case adjudication is pending), and the direction of any label-noise bias is unknown.

The split is random by record with exact-text deduplication only. It has no temporal holdout and no grouping by job control number, so near-duplicate leakage may inflate accuracy, and performance on future records is untested.
Built for post-fix coding: inputs include the corrective action. It is not a pre-repair predictor.
6.8% of records carry codes excluded from the label space (fewer than 5 training examples), so the model cannot predict them.
Single training seed; no run-to-run variance reported.
Training data and model weights are CUI and are not public; results cannot be reproduced externally.
The LLM-written profile narrative (Tab 3) can state details that are not in the data.
blockers_before_featuring: Reconcile the 0.916 frequency-weighted figure with the 0.903 test-split figure, or retire it (README currently headlines 0.903 and flags the conflict)
No baseline measured: maintainer-typed WUC vs QC-corrected label is the decision-relevant one, plus TF-IDF+LR and majority class. Runs on CPU on the authorized box
Commit a non-CUI evidence artifact (counts-only metrics JSON) for each headline figure
Pin requirements.txt and add a synthetic schema sample so the pipeline can be exercised without CUI data
caveat: Accuracy is scored against QC-corrected labels. Training data and model weights are CUI and are not public.
